agree.reason: The 3 a.m. solo shift, the two missed shifts and the nine early mastitis cases make a believable case, but a skeptical reader gets no dollar value, no word on how he would keep working during the program and no contact number, so the letter is less likely to stand out among 150 applicants.

honest.reason: Every specific fact comes from the brief and nothing is invented; 'one of the most dependable people I have employed' is the manager's own judgement and a little generous given the five-week absence, but it is not a factual overstatement.

works_the_facts.reason: The letter repeats the raw facts without deriving anything from them: it never turns two missed shifts out of roughly 780 scheduled into an attendance rate above 99%, and it never says what the nine early mastitis catches meant for the farm.

right_comparison.reason: It gives little sense of how Tomás compares with a typical applicant or with what the program usually expects, apart from saying he is 'already doing the kind of work your program trains people for.'

qualification.reason: A reference letter of this kind does not need conditional claims or hedges with dates attached.

objections.reason: It deals openly with the two likely objections, weak written English and the five-week absence, but the absence is framed as 'two days' notice' with nothing to soften it, and the night class is mentioned without any sign of progress, so a resisting reader's doubts about reliability and coursework are only partly answered.

fit.reason: It is a one-page letter from the farm manager in the right form and tone, but the name, farm and phone number are still placeholders and Tomás's surname is missing.
